response: {"title":"Fastest-falsifier priority","intervention":"Use the remaining verification time only on checks ordered by shortest estimated time to a decisive failure, beginning with syntax/import validation of every changed module and then the smallest targeted test that crosses a changed call boundary; stop verification at 15% of the total deadline.","claim":"Relative to no appended instruction, this bounded fastest-falsifier rule will improve pass_rate without increasing deadline-miss rate and with at most a 5% increase in median wall_time or turns.","mechanism":"Cheap checks rapidly eliminate common catastrophic failures across all edited modules, leaving the bounded residual time for one high-signal integration check rather than low-yield broad testing.","assumptions":["Syntax and import checks are cheap relative to the deadline","Many correctness failures manifest as imports or changed-boundary behavior","The agent can estimate check runtimes approximately"],"risks":["Fast checks can have low semantic coverage","Runtime estimates can be wrong","A 15% cap may be too small for slow test environments","Prioritizing early failures may miss subtle end-to-end regressions"],"test_plan":{"experiment":"On a fixed suite of matched multi-module Python tasks, randomly assign the instruction or no instruction while holding model, seed, tools, and deadline constant; record hidden-test outcome and deadline completion.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"Treatment yields higher pass_rate, no increase in deadline misses, and no more than 5% higher median wall_time and turns."},"single_shot_ordinal":3}
